gate.what: Probe and gate against a real swe-prep clone at the pinned SHA, driven by the committed harvest fixture. This is the surface #22's coverage question is actually about: what a probe can establish and the gate can re-resolve, before ranking spends any of it.
gate.unresolved_are: nine Flow candidates the producer proposed as absent and the gate refused to promote - the atomic quarantine (#35), not a coverage regression. They are the same nine PR 8 measured.

covered.note: 16,488 lines of production source across every source language, where the reference tile counts backend/src/main/java alone. The engine's scope is the whole subject and it says so in the cited command.

Added for this gap. harvest.scale carries production lines only, so this is the one tile the probe measures rather than restates - and it states no figure until the same helper reproduces scale.lines over the production selection.
Added for this gap. 8, the same figure the reference tile carries, off the same one-select discipline as every other tile.
The record half. The engine reads eight resolution comments into decisions and sends the ninth to the gate; the parity suite asserts the count against the reference separately.

The mechanism section is at parity by count (5 against 5) and has been since #7. The engine selects its own five; they are not the reference's five, which is what an independent selection over the same tree looks like.

Two sealed hierarchies with no permitted type in common, and Exercise holding one of each, so all 16 pairings are expressible. The relationship is not a property of either declaration, which is why sealed-hierarchies reporting both closed sets could never carry it.

1 of the 4 types implementing Grader holds a collaborator from the runner package; three hold none, and Grader declares no runner member. Not an odd-one-out, so dependency-asymmetry's held === siblings - 1 test could never see it.

SubmissionOutcome declares every one of Verdict.Outcome's five constants plus SELF_RATED, so a value typed as a machine verdict structurally cannot carry it. The reference's second half - that every competence query filters on outcome = 'PASSED' - is repeated-sql-predicates' finding, minted separately rather than folded in here.

Five of RealContentSmokeTest's five tests call JUnit's assumeTrue, which aborts rather than fails. They are the same five skips the reference records in its ./test.sh excerpt - reached from the tree instead of from a run.

The same two open authoring tickets the reference edge cites, both gate-confirmed absent from the tree. The committed pipeline artifact carries neither, because its live harvest was read later than the pinned fixture and the tracker had moved - which is a fact about the tracker, not about the probe.

unminted.reason: The tile's value is the outcome of a suite RUN - 466 tests, 1 failing, 5 skipped - and #5 makes a probe a pure deterministic function over harvest artifacts with no execution. The declared count is readable from the tree and the self-disabling edge prints its own share of it; the failure is not, and a tile carrying the count alone would drop what the reference tile is for.
unminted.would_need: a stage that builds the subject, which v1 does not have and #5 forecloses for probes

unminted.reason: A package is a Java `package` declaration, and measured-scale is toolchain-neutral by construction: every tile's count and its cited grep are built from ONE shared path select, so the two cannot select different sets. A Java-only tile would have no such shared source, and a directory count is a different figure wearing the same label.
unminted.would_need: a Java fact probe over `declared.ts`'s package clauses, which is buildable and was judged not worth a node type's worth of vocabulary drift here

unminted.reason: NOT a gap in what was established - ci-policy-guards already mints this exact finding, as the mechanism m-ci-guard-ci-yml-test-assert-no-private-content-is-committed, and it survives into the committed artifact. Recasting it as a boundary as well would be one finding minted twice in two vocabularies, which the register's candidate-finding guard exists to refuse.
unminted.would_need: nothing; the finding is present under a different node type

unminted.reason: The statement is what ./test.sh printed, plus a diagnosis of why. A probe may not execute the build (#5), and the diagnosis - readiness reads the wall clock where every other date-sensitive service reads the injected one - is a comparison a grep can suggest and only a reader can settle.
unminted.would_need: a build-running stage, which #5 forecloses for probes

unminted.reason: The mechanism is built and is the one #7 point 7 requires: decided-but-unbuilt hands the gate `expect: "absent"` claims for open tickets and the gate overturns them where the tree says otherwise. The INSTANCE is gone - #26 is closed in the pinned harvest - so the subject no longer exhibits it. Producing it anyway would mean asserting an issue state the record does not carry.
unminted.would_need: nothing; the producer exists and the subject moved

unminted.reason: The finding is that a resolution comment specifies a domain the tree does not carry. Locating that specification inside an argument that also names rejected alternatives is a prose judgement, and #2 gives reading a decision record to the write stage's model alone; its `decided_not_built` path is the producer. On this subject the model settled every decision it read as built.
unminted.would_need: the write stage to reach this comment, not a new probe

unminted.reason: Same shape as e-frontend-domain: a section of a resolution comment specifying work the tree does not carry, which only the write stage may read.
unminted.would_need: the write stage to reach this comment, not a new probe

unminted.reason: dependency-divergence compares the README against the declared build manifests, and swe-prep's README names neither JPA nor Lombok - the divergence lives in decision #2's resolution comment. Extending the probe to scan resolution comments for technology names would report a REJECTED alternative as a divergence, because telling the chosen stack from the rejected ones is exactly the prose judgement #2 reserves for the write stage. That is the #28 defect shape - vocabulary matched against raw lines - and the gate could not catch it, because it would confirm the manifest half of a claim whose record half nothing checked.
unminted.would_need: the write stage, which already settles implementation claims against the tree

unminted.reason: A tradeoff argued in a resolution comment, with a timeout property and a captured-output cap as corroboration. The constants are readable; that they add up to a deliberate decision not to sandbox is the record's argument, which only the write stage reads.
unminted.would_need: the write stage to reach this comment, not a new probe

unminted.reason: The finding is an argument made in javadoc across five services - that derived state is recomputed per request rather than stored. Recognising that from prose is a model judgement; a probe that matched the vocabulary would be asserting a design stance out of a comment, which is the defect #28 closed.
unminted.would_need: the write stage, or a probe over the shared-state Flow producer's own reads, which would establish the reads and not the stance

unminted.reason: tuned-config-properties reads .yml/.properties/.toml/.ini/.conf/.json for a setting whose comment marks it as measured. This one is an XML <systemPropertyVariables> entry under a comment that carries no such marker - it explains a Testcontainers probe workaround without saying anything was measured or tuned. Adding XML alone would not reach it; widening the vocabulary until it did is the 'matched policy vocabulary against any raw line' failure #28 closed.
unminted.would_need: a judgement about what a comment means, which is the write stage's, not a probe's

beyond_the_reference.what: Boundaries the new probes establish that the hand-made overview does not carry. Parity is the bar, not the ceiling: an independent reading of the same tree finds its own seams.

committed_artifact.what: The committed end-to-end artifact (swe-prep.pipeline.atlas.json) predates these probes and still reports 18 nodes. It is NOT regenerated here, and the reason is a constraint rather than an omission.
committed_artifact.why_not_regenerated: rank refuses to run on an unscored node (MissingScoreError: 'an unscored node is not a zero, it is a node nobody judged'), so eight new gate-confirmed candidates cannot reach an artifact without a fresh `repo-atlas score` run - a credentialed model call this task did not make. Reassembling from the pinned score file would fail, correctly.
committed_artifact.recommended_follow_up: run `repo-atlas score` and then `repo-atlas run` against the pinned subject, refresh swe-prep.pipeline.{written,scores,gated,atlas}.json, and move the node-count pin to what that run measures.
